mode achieved: static review; read every e2e/web spec and helper, one Maestro flow, playwright.config.ts, every scripts/*.test.* and eslint-rules/*.test.js, the gate scripts (verify, canary, check-trace, check-web-release, serve-web), jest.config.js, stryker.config.json, knip.jsonc, package.json scripts, .github/workflows/check.yml, reports/verify.md, spec sections 9 to 11 and the flake note; ran one python count (Vietnamese lines) and one node probe of check-trace.mjs's exported functions in the scratchpad; ran no gate (Stryker run in progress)
verdict: 2 blockers, 9 majors, 3 nits. The tooling unit tests are strong; the gate system has no floor on what counts as traced, what ran, what reached the network, and which tree a green report describes.

🔴 blocker  The trace gate passes with no running test: skipped, todo and fixme titles count, and a code is matched against every screen's tests
- key: scripts/check-trace.mjs#vacuous-trace
- where: spec 9.1 rule 5 (spec lines 421-422); scripts/check-trace.mjs:12-21 (CALLS and rootName accept any test.* chain), :43-45, :60-65 (untraced matches each code against one global title list), :84-88
- why: (1) a title on test.skip, test.todo, test.fixme or an empty describe satisfies the rule; scripts/check-trace.test.mjs:13-15 and :21-31 pin `test.skip('OVW-02 skipped')` and `it.only` as valid titles, so the vacuity is asserted as intended. (2) the 491 titles of src and e2e are pooled, so a second screen that lists a BRD-wide code (D-19 "usable on phones", BR-32) is traced by screen 24's tests; narrow.spec.ts alone has 36 titles starting with D-19. Multiplier: every contract.yaml plan C adds. probe: node import of titlesOf and untraced from scripts/check-trace.mjs (scratchpad trace_probe.mjs, 2026-10-09): a fake contract 26-wbs-table with [BR-32, D-19] and no test of its own returned [] (fully traced); codes WBS-01 to WBS-04 whose only titles were test.skip, test.todo, test.fixme and an empty describe returned [].
- trigger: plan C adds src/screens/26-wbs-table/contract.yaml with `requirements: [WBS-01, BR-32, D-19]` and one `test.skip('WBS-01 ...')`; gate:trace exits 0 and prints that every code has a test; screen 26 has zero running tests for its three requirements.
- guard-bypass: the trace canary (scripts/canary.mjs:142-146) only plants a code that no title names; Jest and Playwright report a skipped test as skipped and exit 0; eslint.config.js has no focused or disabled test rule.
- fix: in check-trace.mjs ignore call chains containing skip, todo or fixme; count a describe title only as a prefix of the test or it titles nested in it; scope titles per screen, so a code of screen S counts only from files under src/screens/S/ or e2e/web/S/ (move the screen 24 specs into e2e/web/24-project-overview/). Add both cases to check-trace.test.mjs and a trace-skip canary.
- approach-changing: no, the gate stays a title scan; only its filter and scope change
- design: yes, per-screen title scope and a skip-aware title walk

🔴 blocker  A request that escapes the mock server is invisible to 60 of the 75 browser tests that open the app; the one recorded escape was deferred, not diagnosed
- key: e2e/web/support.ts#no-request-guard
- where: implicit precondition of every browser test, that each call to https://api.metis.test is answered by the MSW service worker (e2e/web/mocks.spec.ts:8); src/platform/mocks.web.ts:12-15; plan/2026-10-09-frontend-trace-and-gaps.md lines 61-67
- why: MSW starts with `onUnhandledRequest: 'bypass', quiet: true` (mocks.web.ts:13-14), so an unhandled or missed call goes to the real network with no log. Failures are observed only where a test opts into pageErrors (support.ts:87-94): routes.spec.ts:40, states.spec.ts:114 (12 tests), language.spec.ts:95, controls.spec.ts:149, i.e. 15 of the 75 tests that open the app. The other 60 (narrow 36, shape 4, brand 4, controls.pages 3, controls 5, language 2, mocks 3, routes 3) record neither console errors nor failed requests, and brand.spec.ts:75 explicitly counts api.metis.test as "inside", so the only test that logs every request cannot see an escape. The plan recorded one escape (`net::ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED` in routes.spec), calls the mechanism an untested hypothesis and defers the diagnosis to a "next step"; the whole browser layer rests on that unresolved assumption.
- trigger: under load the worker misses the shell call (as recorded once), or a plan C screen calls an endpoint with no handler; the call fails DNS; a narrow.spec or shape.spec test measures a page whose sidebar or panel is in an error state and passes (its oracles look for overflow, and an emptier page overflows less), or fails as an unexplained flake.
- guard-bypass: pageErrors is opt-in per test and there is no shared fixture; quiet: true silences MSW; bypass makes an unhandled path legal.
- fix: export a `test` from e2e/web/support.ts built with base.extend and one auto fixture, and import it in every spec instead of '@playwright/test'; the fixture fails the test, naming the URL, on any requestfailed event and on any response for hostname api.metis.test whose fromServiceWorker() is false [Source: node_modules/playwright-core/types/types.d.ts:22566-22570], and on any page error the test did not declare (states.spec.ts's console column becomes that declaration). In the e2e build replace 'bypass' with a callback strategy that raises only for api.metis.test [Source: node_modules/msw/lib/core/utils/request/onUnhandledRequest.d.ts:6 allows a callback; onUnhandledRequest.mjs:19-25 shows 'error' logs and throws] [Unverified - confirm the callback signature of MSW 2.15 before applying].
- approach-changing: no, one shared fixture; spec bodies stay
- design: yes, an auto fixture that owns network and console observability for every spec

🟡 major  CI cannot finish: both jobs stop at 30 minutes, the mutation gate alone measured 75, and the mutation canary runs it twice
- key: .github/workflows/check.yml#timeout-below-mutation
- where: .github/workflows/check.yml:27 and :52 (timeout-minutes: 30), :42 (pnpm verify), :64 (pnpm canary all); package.json gate:mutation = `stryker run`; scripts/canary.mjs:183 and :191; spec 11.1 (spec lines 487-498)
- why: reports/verify.md measures gate:mutation at 4,527.2 s on the 10-core Mac with 5 runners (75 min); the earlier run took 60 min 13 s (trace-and-gaps plan line 73). The verify job runs every gate:* in sequence, so it is cancelled inside gate:mutation on every run. runCanary runs the gate once for the green baseline and once after planting, so the mutation canary costs two full runs inside a 30-minute job. Spec 11.1 puts "mutation on changed code" on each pull request and the full run on the schedule; gate:mutation implements only the full run. What the hour bought, measured: the trace-and-gaps run left 0 survivors (1,363 killed, 31 timeouts); the final run left 1 survivor, an equivalent mutant closed by a Stryker disable pair (verify.md last paragraphs); no recorded full run led to a new assertion. check.yml:39-40 says the workflow has never run, so nothing has shown this yet.
- trigger: first push to GitHub: the verify job is cancelled at 30:00 inside gate:mutation and every pull request is red; the Monday canary job is cancelled inside the mutation canary.
- guard-bypass: the workflow never ran (check.yml:39-40); verify.mjs has no per-gate time budget.
- fix: per pull request run `stryker run --incremental` [Source: node_modules/@stryker-mutator/core/schema/stryker-schema.json:357-360, "Stryker will store results in a file and use that file to speed up the next --incremental run"] with the incremental file cached between CI runs [Unverified - confirm the cache step]; move the full run to a mutation:full script in the scheduled job with a timeout above the measured 75 min; make the mutation canary pass `--mutate src/core/canary-weak.ts` so it costs seconds.
- approach-changing: no, it restores the split spec 11.1 already specifies
- design: yes, an incremental mutation gate and a separate scheduled full run

🟡 major  Nothing fails when browser tests stop running: test.only passes on the Mac, skips pass everywhere, and the report keeps no count
- key: apps/metis/playwright.config.ts#no-run-floor
- where: gate:web (package.json); playwright.config.ts:8; scripts/verify.mjs:56; reports/verify.md
- why: `forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI` (playwright.config.ts:8) is off in pnpm verify on the Mac (verify.mjs:56 passes the inherited environment and sets no CI), the run spec 11.2 places before each pull request; Playwright then runs only the focused tests and exits 0 [Source: node_modules/playwright/types/test.d.ts:1276-1294]. test.skip and test.fixme exit 0 in any environment. A spec file that stops matching drops out silently: only narrow.spec.ts carries a requirement code the trace gate would miss; states, routes, language, brand, mocks and shape carry none. eslint.config.js has no focused or disabled test rule (grep: 0 lines); today there are 0 .only, .skip, .todo or .fixme calls outside check-trace's own fixtures, so nothing is broken yet. verify.md stores exit codes only: the browser count moved 100, 108, 160 (trace-and-gaps plan line 74; verify.md last paragraph) with no machine record, so a drop from 160 to 2 reads the same.
- trigger: a developer leaves test.only on one narrow.spec test; pnpm verify on the Mac runs 2 browser tests (one per browser) instead of 160 and writes `gate:web | green`. NOT RUN: Stryker run in progress; proof command: add .only to one test in a scratch copy, then `cd apps/metis && pnpm test:e2e`.
- guard-bypass: forbidOnly is CI-only; coverage and mutation never observe Playwright; the report has no count.
- fix: playwright.config.ts:8 `forbidOnly: true`; add a JSON reporter (`reporter: [['list'], ['json', { outputFile: 'reports/e2e.json' }]]`) and make verify.mjs fail gate:web when the run reports any skipped test or fewer passed tests than a committed floor; add no-focused and no-disabled test lint rules for src/**/*.test.* and e2e/**.
- approach-changing: no, config plus a count check
- design: yes, a test-count floor recorded by verify

🟡 major  The browser layout oracles are negative checks with no positive control and no population count, and gate:web has no canary
- key: e2e/web/narrow.spec.ts#negative-oracles-unproven
- where: D-19 and spec 4.4 checks clipped (support.ts:63-76), overflowing (support.ts:50-57), smallTargets (narrow.spec.ts:68-86), outsideFrames (narrow.spec.ts:254-278), all asserted toEqual([]) (narrow.spec.ts:28-29, 122, 138, 288, 295; shape.spec.ts:83-84)
- why: each helper returns the bad elements of a population it never counts, so a shrinking population reads as a pass. support.spec.ts self-tests token, px, rgb, box, style, blockingAxe and pageErrors (support.spec.ts:6-49) but none of these four. The text population is [dir="auto"], which react-native-web sets only on a root Text with neither dir nor lang (node_modules/react-native-web/dist/exports/Text/index.js:101-108); no shipped Text sets lang or dir today (grep: 0), so the oracles are complete now and go blind the day one does. smallTargets defines a control with its own selector (narrow.spec.ts:72-73) that lacks the [tabindex="0"] of INTERACTIVE (support.ts:46-47), so a Pressable without a role is never measured (every Pressable in the 16 shipped files the grep showed sets a role today). gate:web has no canary (scripts/canary.mjs:16-147 covers lint, tokens, deadcode, unit, mutation, types, format, trace; the spec 10 rows for shape, behaviour, reverse check, translation, brand and the 44 px target are deferred per reports/review/spec-gaps.md lines 397-402), and the reverse tests of R-T12 and R-N34 were one-off manual edits (trace-and-gaps plan lines 57-60; narrow-widths plan lines 219-226) that nobody can rerun.
- trigger: a Vietnamese typography fix passes lang={locale} to the design-system Text; root Texts render dir="ltr" instead of dir="auto"; a label clipped at 360 px is no longer scanned by clipped or outsideFrames; the 36 D-19 tests stay green.
- guard-bypass: the only positive controls ran once by hand; language.spec.ts:70-71 has a positive control, but it protects only that file's textsOf.
- fix: move the four helpers into support.ts returning { checked, bad } and assert checked above a per-page floor beside each bad assertion; select text by [dir] instead of [dir="auto"]; use INTERACTIVE in smallTargets; add one support.spec.ts case per helper with page.setContent holding a clipped text, a 30 px button and an overflowing box (the shape of the axe self-test at support.spec.ts:33-42); add a touch-target canary for gate:web that plants a 30 px target (spec line 472), and a canary.test.mjs check that every gate:* has a canary or a listed reason (gate:web, gate:tooling and gate:deps have none).
- approach-changing: no, helpers gain a count and a self-test
- design: yes, a helper contract with population counts, helper self-tests and a gate-to-canary meta check

🟡 major  reports/verify.md says gate:mutation is red; the green status is hand-written prose, and the report is not bound to the tree it tested
- key: scripts/verify.mjs#report-not-bound-to-tree
- where: reports/verify.md (table and the two paragraphs under it); scripts/verify.mjs:11-17, :30-44, :65
- why: the machine table reads `gate:mutation | RED | 4527.2`. Green rests on two hand-added paragraphs (a Stryker run limited to src/shell/Shell.tsx, then a rerun of the ten other gates) that verify.mjs:65 overwrites on the next run. The report carries `Commit: no commit yet` (the verify.mjs:15 fallback) and no dirty-tree marker, content hash or per-gate test count, so it cannot show which code was green. The brief for this review reads it as "every gate green, 2,639 Jest tests, 108 Playwright tests" while the file says mutation red, 2,663 and 160: the report is already being misread. A one-file mutation rerun is fair evidence for a Stryker disable pair, but no machine record of it exists.
- trigger: edit any src file after the run; verify.md still shows the same rows and prose; the owner's review package cites it as green.
- guard-bypass: commitOf reads HEAD only (verify.mjs:11-17) and the repo has no commits; nothing ties prose to a run.
- fix: verify.mjs writes a Tree line (a hash over the contents of `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard` plus the count of `git status --porcelain` lines), adds per-gate counts parsed from `jest --json` and the Playwright JSON report, and accepts `--only <gate>` that appends a machine-written rerun row with its own tree hash instead of prose.
- approach-changing: no, report fields only
- design: yes, a tree hash and a machine rerun row

🟡 major  The release check restates four fixture strings by hand and never proves they occur in a mock build; renaming the fixtures blinds it
- key: scripts/check-web-release.mjs#markers-restated
- where: spec 3.4 (the release web export carries no mock server or mock data); scripts/check-web-release.mjs:10-18; scripts/check-web-release.test.mjs:29-47, :56-94; package.json build:web and gate:web
- why: 'Northwind Furniture Co.', 'Creative Production', 'Denny K.' and 'Acme Holdings' are copies of src/mocks/fixtures/showroom.ts:11-15, meridian.ts:12-16 and shell.ts:32. The tests feed synthetic files containing the same literals, so they prove the scanner, never that the markers still occur in the fixtures or in a build that holds them; no step runs findMocks on dist-e2e, the one build known to contain the mocks. Renaming the fixture data, the obvious answer to the owner's complaint about "Northwind Furniture Co.", leaves 4 of 7 markers matching nothing while every test stays green.
- trigger: rename the fixture client and PM; later a src/platform module imports a fixture outside the EXPO_PUBLIC_MOCKS block (eslint.config.js:157-158 allows src/platform to import src/mocks); `pnpm build:web` prints `OK dist`.
- guard-bypass: the three MSW markers catch MSW code, not fixture data; the lint boundary allows src/platform; the unit tests use their own literals.
- fix: build the fixture markers from src/mocks/fixtures/*.ts with the TypeScript parser check-trace.mjs already imports (check-trace.mjs:9; every string literal of 12 characters or more), and add a positive control to gate:web after build:web:e2e: `node scripts/check-web-release.mjs dist-e2e --expect-all` must report every marker, so a stale marker fails the gate.
- approach-changing: no
- design: yes, derived markers plus a positive-control run on dist-e2e

🟡 major  The browser specs type route paths, dictionary copy and fixture values by hand; the hand-copied routes table lets new destinations go untested
- key: e2e/web#restated-literals
- where: every e2e/web spec; sources of truth src/core/routes.ts:5-28 (ROUTES), src/mocks/fixtures/*.ts, the strings dictionaries
- why: counts (grep over e2e and scripts): meridian-cgi-campaign on 13 lines in 11 files; creative-studio on 30 lines of e2e; the overview path constant redefined in 8 specs (narrow.spec.ts:8, routes.spec.ts:5-6, controls.pages.spec.ts:15-16, controls.spec.ts:10, language.spec.ts:13, brand.spec.ts:9, states.spec.ts:6, shape.spec.ts:6) and inlined in mocks.spec.ts:22. 32 selector or assertion lines in 5 specs type dictionary copy (brand 4, language 12, states 8, narrow 7, controls 1: 'Open menu', 'Mo menu', 'Main', 'Registry', 'Overview', 'Tong quan', 'Language', 'Ngon ngu', 'Not baselined', 'Stale', 'Your session expired', 'Page not found', `Screen ${screen}`; e.g. narrow.spec.ts:132, :291, states.spec.ts:70, language.spec.ts:86, controls.spec.ts:80), although the suite already has the mechanism (controls.pages.spec.ts:56-62 reads STRINGS.en; language.spec.ts:5-9 imports both dictionaries). Fixture values: '12' (shape.spec.ts:55, controls.spec.ts:95, states.spec.ts:29) and 'Northwind Furniture Co.' (narrow.spec.ts:218, the client at src/mocks/fixtures/meridian.ts:12). Also restated: the 403 console line (controls.spec.ts:13 and states.spec.ts:12-13), the storage key 'metis.locale' (open.ts:17, language.spec.ts:104, mocks.spec.ts:39 against src/platform/storage.web.ts:6), token values (support.spec.ts:7-11 and gen-tokens.test.mjs:97-104), the contract's requirement list (contract.spec.ts:9-19 against contract.yaml:8), the logo width 68.578125 (brand.spec.ts:122, derivable from px('logo-h') and the viewBox). All of these fail loudly when the source changes (maintenance: one copy edit touches up to 32 lines) except the routes table: routes.spec.ts:9-32 hand-copies 21 of the 22 ROUTES keys, so a destination plan C adds to ROUTES gets no deep-link test.
- trigger: plan C adds a destination to ROUTES and its route file; routes.spec.ts PLACEHOLDERS is not updated; a deep link that crashes is not caught unless the sidebar links it (controls.spec.ts:147-169).
- guard-bypass: nothing derives e2e paths or copy from src; ROUTES reaches e2e only through SCREENS in links.ts:4.
- fix: one e2e/web/app.ts exporting pathOf(destination, params) built from ROUTES and the fixture ids (creativeStudio, meridian, showroom), text(locale, key) read from the dictionaries (generalise controls.pages.spec.ts:56-62) and fixture-derived figures; routes.spec.ts iterates Object.keys(ROUTES) minus the built destinations.
- approach-changing: no
- design: yes, a shared e2e data module

🟡 major  The "text lays out like iOS and Android" gate is a CSS stand-in calibrated on the one defect it was built from, and no gate runs the native flows
- key: e2e/web/narrow.spec.ts#yoga-emulation-in-sample
- where: narrow.spec.ts:249-299 (16 tests per browser, 32 in all); plan/2026-10-09-frontend-narrow-widths.md R-N34 (lines 219-226) and R-N28 (line 186); e2e/native/*.yaml; spec 11.2 (spec lines 502-503)
- why: the gate injects `[dir="auto"] { flex-shrink: 0 !important; max-width: 100%; }` (narrow.spec.ts:253) and stands for the native layout. R-N34 records that it was derived from the single measured Android overflow (41 px at 800 dp), that max-width: 100% was added after the emulation flagged a text that wraps correctly on the device, and that its reverse test removes that same fix (6 red cases at 768, 800, 900): both calibrations are in-sample. R-N28 records a second native-only difference (Yoga on iOS ignoring flexBasis in a row) that this emulation does not model. The native flows check visibility of a few ids (tablet.yaml:12-44) and no gate runs them (package.json has no native gate; verify.mjs:9 runs gate:* only), though spec 11.2 puts the Maestro flows on the iOS Simulator inside pnpm verify.
- trigger: plan C adds a row whose native overflow comes from a Yoga rule other than text flex-shrink (the R-N28 class); the 32 web tests pass and nothing native runs before review.
- guard-bypass: the Maestro flows are manual (reports/review/review.md line 357 lists the contract-generated flows as missing); the web emulation has no out-of-sample check.
- fix: add a gate:native on the Mac (spec 11.2) that runs e2e/native/phone.yaml and tablet.yaml and asserts the same no-overflow property on device, or rename the 32 tests to what they measure (CSS flex-shrink emulation) and list the native layout check as an open spec item at the top of review.md (rule FE-23).
- approach-changing: no, it adds the gate spec 11.2 already names
- design: yes, a native layout gate

🟡 major  The lines that turn gate results into exit codes are excluded from coverage and untested for verify, canary and check-trace
- key: scripts/verify.mjs#cli-exit-unpinned
- where: scripts/verify.mjs:46-69, scripts/canary.mjs:204-226, scripts/check-trace.mjs:98-103 (all inside node:coverage disable); package.json gate:tooling (100% thresholds); .github/workflows/check.yml:42, :64
- why: verify.mjs:56 (`.status === 0`) and :67 (`process.exitCode = code`), canary.mjs:217-219 and :224, and check-trace.mjs:101 decide what CI sees, and no test executes them, so gate:tooling's 100% says nothing about them. check-web-release.test.mjs:96-106 and serve-web.test.mjs:78-85 already pin their CLIs by spawning them; verify.test.mjs tests only verify() (verify.test.mjs:17-43).
- trigger: a refactor deletes verify.mjs:67 or changes :56 to compare against null; pnpm verify exits 0 with a red row; the CI job is green.
- guard-bypass: coverage is disabled for exactly these lines and no spawn test exists.
- fix: add spawn tests on the check-web-release pattern: run verify.mjs with cwd in a temp dir whose package.json has `"gate:a": "node -e \"process.exit(1)\""` and `"gate:b": "node -e \"\""`, assert exit status 1 and the `| gate:a | RED |` row in reports/verify.md; run canary.mjs against a temp root with a fake gate; run check-trace.mjs on a temp tree with one untraced code and assert exit 1.
- approach-changing: no

🟡 major  Test titles, tool output and comments of the browser and tooling layers are Vietnamese, and 22 test lines pin the Vietnamese output
- key: apps/metis/e2e+scripts#vietnamese-in-tests-and-tools
- where: e2e/web, e2e/native, scripts, eslint-rules, playwright.config.ts, jest.config.js, stryker.config.json, knip.jsonc
- why: scan with the brief's diacritic class over this scope (python, scratchpad vi_scan.py): 505 lines in 45 files: 338 comments, 98 test titles (all 42 title lines of e2e/web, 54 of 56 in scripts tests, 2 of 2 in eslint-rules tests), 69 strings and tool output (verify report `green`, `RED`, `| Gate | Result | Seconds |`, `no commit yet` at verify.mjs:15, :32, :39; canary log lines canary.mjs:185, :198-199, :216; check-trace.mjs:91, :94; check-web-release.mjs:42; serve-web.mjs:53; the no-style-literals messages), and 26 comment lines in the gate config files. 22 lines of script tests assert the Vietnamese output (e.g. verify.test.mjs:57-60, canary.test.mjs:67, :82, :107, check-trace.test.mjs:89-90, no-style-literals.test.js:153-155), so translating the output means editing those tests. 39 lines cite plan or spec ids (R-B19, D-B27, R-T12, spec 4.4). The default-text canary expects the string `spec 5.5` inside a lint message (canary.mjs:135), so cleaning spec citations out of messages will make that canary fail. The only legitimate Vietnamese here is vi-locale test data ('Tong quan', 'Ngon ngu', 'Mo menu'), which the restated-literals fix moves to the vi dictionary. No regression slips through; the cost is that an agency developer reads a red gate (Playwright title, verify.md, canary log) in Vietnamese, and every new spec copies the convention.
- trigger: an agency developer gets `canary token-literal: gate:lint did NOT catch the planted defect (exit code 0)` or the failing title `D-19 360 px vi language: one column, no horizontal scroll, tap targets of at least touch size` and cannot tell what failed.
- guard-bypass: no check rejects Vietnamese outside the dictionaries.
- fix: English titles that keep the requirement code first (check-trace.mjs:53-57 needs it; e.g. `D-19 360 px vi: one column, no horizontal scroll, 44 px targets`), English tool output with the pinned test lines updated, a one-line why instead of plan ids; the default-text canary expects its rule id instead of `spec 5.5`; a scripts/language.test.mjs in gate:tooling that scans src, e2e, scripts, eslint-rules and the root configs with the brief's diacritic class and allows only src/**/strings/vi.ts.
- approach-changing: no
- design: yes, a diacritic scan in gate:tooling with an allowlist

💭 nit  On the Mac, Playwright reuses whatever server holds port 5310, whichever checkout it serves
- key: apps/metis/playwright.config.ts#reuse-server
- where: playwright.config.ts:3-4, :18-22
- why: with CI unset, reuseExistingServer is true, so the webServer command is skipped when 127.0.0.1:5310 answers and E2E_DIST is ignored.
